notes: Round 2 correctly and verifiably fixes the round-1 blocking finding, but a live scratch test this round surfaces a second, pre-existing identity-check gap in the same safety mechanism (project_tree_bind_state, unmodified this round) that lets a foreign mount be silently misclassified as the script's own correct bind whenever the ext4 target directory has never yet been created -- the exact situation on a project's very first ensure. Requesting one more round to close that gap before approval, since it sits in the same rc==2 detection path this round's fix depends on and is visible to anyone running ensure/status, not just a rare tooling corner case.

ROUND1-FIX-CORRECT.detail: Re-read project_tree_ensure_dir (:216-266): bind_rc==0 short-circuits ('already bound'), bind_rc==2 now warns and returns before either the mkdir/mount block or the --dry-run branch is reached ('skip $link_path: already a mountpoint bound to something other than $ext4_dir -- leaving it alone'), matching project_tree_release_dir's own project_tree_same_directory-based posture. The now-dead 'would rebind' dry-run text is gone; project_tree_usage's ensure description was reworded to state the new posture ('A dir already mounted from something other than its ext4 directory is left alone (skip + warn), never force-unmounted or taken over.'). No other function's code changed (diff-equivalent read of the whole file against the round-1 version confirms only project_tree_ensure_dir and project_tree_usage differ).

ROUND1-FIX-INDEPENDENTLY-VERIFIED-LIVE.detail: Reproduced the reviewer's own repro in WSL Debian (root, ext4 scratch under /opt, not tmpfs/NTFS): created a real bind (ensure), released it (ext4 dir kept on disk), placed a genuine foreign `mount --bind` on node_modules, then ran `ensure` again with vendor also pending in the same call. Result: node_modules stayed bound to the foreign source (confirmed by reading back the foreign marker file's content through the mount afterward) while vendor was bound normally in the same run ('[project-tree] bound .../vendor -> ...'); `ensure --dry-run` against the same foreign mount printed only the skip/warning, never a rebind claim; final `mount` sweep showed nothing left over after cleanup. Matches the round-2 report's own verification narrative exactly.

BIND-STATE-IDENTITY-GAP.detail: project_tree_bind_state (:194-201, unchanged this round) only compares device+inode when `[ -d "$ext4_dir" ]` is already true; when the ext4 target directory has never been created (a project's first-ever ensure/status call), the identity check is skipped entirely and the function returns 0 ('bound', meaning verified-correct) for ANY existing mountpoint at the link path, foreign or not. Live-reproduced in WSL Debian: fresh scratch repo, node_modules never ensured before (ext4_dir does not exist on disk), a genuine unrelated `mount --bind` placed directly on node_modules. `status` then reports 'node_modules ... bound -> <ext4_dir>' (implying the intended isolation is correctly active) even though <ext4_dir> does not exist and the mount source is a completely different directory; `ensure` reports 'already bound: node_modules -> <ext4_dir>' and takes no action at all -- so the real ext4 directory and bind for that project+dir are silently never created, on every future run, until an operator notices by hand. The comment directly above the function already signals awareness of this ('rc 0 = bound, and (when it can be verified) it is exactly ext4_dir') but resolves the unverifiable case to the less safe default (assume match) instead of the safer one project_tree_same_directory/project_tree_release_dir already use elsewhere in this same file (treat 'cannot verify' as 'not the same', which safely lands in the already-implemented bind_rc==2 skip+warn branch). This does not cause any NTFS write or takeover (fails toward inaction, not toward harm), so it is not the same severity as the round-1 finding, but it undermines the very identity check this round's fix is built on top of, and both ensure and status give false-positive success signals in a plain, first-run scenario -- not an exotic corner case. Minimal fix: make the 'cannot verify because ext4_dir does not exist yet' case return 2 (or a distinct code treated the same way as 2 by ensure/status) instead of falling through to 0, so a mountpoint at the link path is only ever treated as 'ours' when it can actually be confirmed.

NTFS-SAFETY.detail: No path -- including the newly exercised bind_rc==2 skip branch and the BIND-STATE-IDENTITY-GAP false-positive branch above -- writes, deletes or creates anything under the in-repo (potentially NTFS) directory or moves/removes the mount source found there. Both the round-1 gap and the new gap found this round fail toward doing nothing, never toward an unsafe write or takeover.
